nodes.label: guided (60 Hz cue synthesizer)

nodes.norm_label: bridge (udp in, websocket out, jsonl recording)

nodes.label: Beacon (chest-worn item-homing wearable)
nodes.rationale: On-device, no tags, a supplement to a cane: homes a blind or low-vision wearer to a named item by spoken bearing then stereo ticks.

nodes.label: Pre-rendered Speech Clips (16 kHz mono WAV per clip id)
nodes.norm_label: pre-rendered speech clips (16 khz mono wav per clip id)

nodes.label: voiced (speech to intent)

nodes.label: --metres Spoken Metres Gate
nodes.rationale: Metres are spoken only after the tape-measure check passes (spec Section 11); off by default.

nodes.label: Newest-wins Dashboard Backpressure (skip clients >1 MB behind)
nodes.norm_label: newest-wins dashboard backpressure (skip clients >1 mb behind)
nodes.rationale: Nothing queues, so a slow dashboard never delays others.

nodes.label: NO DATA Staleness Indicator (1 s)
nodes.rationale: Shown when no world state arrived for 1 s so a frozen screen never looks LIVE.

nodes.label: Branch-per-owner PR Workflow
nodes.rationale: main holds the shared base; never commit sd-stage/ (network secrets) or large model files.

nodes.label: Freeze beacon.h from nathans-revision Section 6
nodes.rationale: intent.kind must include REPEAT and REJECT; CAM_W/CAM_H must not be frozen from the C270 webcam.

nodes.label: Hold-then-Lost Cue (never a guessed metre)
nodes.rationale: When the detector dies the ticks hold, then a lost cue is spoken, instead of guessing a distance.

nodes.label: Monitoring Isolated from the Wearer's Path
nodes.norm_label: monitoring isolated from the wearer's path
nodes.rationale: Never writes shm, never talks to guided, not a cloud path; killing it must not change what the wearer hears.

nodes.label: Ultralytics AGPL-3.0 Licence Risk
nodes.rationale: Ultralytics weights and code are AGPL-3.0; an embedded commercial or closed-source product needs an Enterprise licence.

nodes.label: CLIP / MobileCLIP2 Region Retrieval
nodes.rationale: 200-265 ms per encode on Pi 5 CPU costs as much as another detector; the fast ExecuTorch variant is not packaged for QNX, so it stays off the hot loop and out of v1.

nodes.label: ONNX Runtime 1.24.4 on QNX
nodes.rationale: ONNX is the fastest documented model format actually available on QNX; historically needed manual patches, so even the packaged version deserves an early smoke test on the loaner.

nodes.label: YOLO-World INT8 TFLite
nodes.rationale: Credible speed play via onnx2tf INT8 and QNX tflite-runtime 2.21.0, but calibration, off-target export and header/version mismatch make it a bench experiment, not the weekend path.

nodes.label: YOLO-Worldv2-s ONNX
nodes.rationale: Viable via ORT but strictly worse than YOLOE for this budget: larger checkpoint, no published Pi timing, prompts fixed at export; kept as fallback.

nodes.label: YOLOE-26n-seg (text-prompted, baked static ONNX)
nodes.rationale: Saturday pick: the only family with real text-defined open vocabulary and a plausible Pi 5 CPU budget; prompt embeddings fold into a normal YOLO head so no text encoder ships to the Pi. Open vocabulary means prompt-defined labels at export, fixed at runtime.

nodes.label: YOLOE-26n-seg-pf (prompt-free, 4,585 names)
nodes.rationale: Stretch only if Phase 3 is green: labels anything walked past without re-export, but full-vocabulary region-text comparison adds ~89% CPU time and LVIS mAP is low.

nodes.label: Find My Things (Morrison et al., ASSETS 2023)
nodes.norm_label: find my things (morrison et al., assets 2023)

nodes.label: Baked 16-32 Noun Vocabulary Limitation
nodes.rationale: A baked 16-32 label list with no retraining is a product limitation to disclose; cultural and personal items are documented misfit sources and 'keys' must map to a label the detector actually produces.

nodes.label: Do-Not-Attempt Models (Grounding DINO, DINO-X, Florence-2, Moondream, Qwen2-VL, NanoOWL)
nodes.norm_label: do-not-attempt models (grounding dino, dino-x, florence-2, moondream, qwen2-vl, nanoowl)
nodes.rationale: Seconds to tens of seconds per frame on Pi CPU, API-only (cloud, which the prize rejects), or CUDA/TensorRT-only; none fit the weekend runtime.

nodes.label: Host-Side Model Export (x86/macOS laptop)
nodes.rationale: Ultralytics LiteRT export refuses Linux ARM64, and the 254 MB mobileclip2 text encoder should never ship to the Pi, so prompt baking and ONNX export happen once on a laptop.

nodes.label: Loaner Pi p50/p95 Deciding Measurement
nodes.rationale: All Pi 5 numbers are Linux proxies; decide between text-prompted and prompt-free YOLOE by p50/p95 end-to-end detector time over 200 frames on QNX ORT with the full pipeline running, plus at least 8/10 correct labels.

nodes.label: QNX AI Runtime Packaging Constraint
nodes.rationale: QNX ports ONNX Runtime, MediaPipe, OpenCV and TFLite but not NCNN, ExecuTorch, TensorRT or RKNN; NCNN is fastest on ARM Linux but unavailable here, so a weekend port is not credible.

nodes.label: Beacon (chest-worn named-object homing device)
nodes.rationale: Homing cue for a named item seen this session so a blind or low-vision wearer need not wait for a sighted helper; supplement to the cane; sighted-team prototype, not BLV-tested.

nodes.label: Henomaly (process split + ORT on Pi 5 QNX)
nodes.norm_label: henomaly (process split + ort on pi 5 qnx)

nodes.label: telemd optional monitoring process
nodes.rationale: Read-only world-state JSON + downscaled JPEG to a local laptop; kill it and the wearer hears no difference; never cloud.

nodes.label: Beacon spec adversarial review
nodes.rationale: Review-only of an earlier draft; contract holes were patched in docs/nathans-revision.md. Do not implement from this review.

nodes.label: Beacon: Nathan's revision (spec)
nodes.rationale: Implementation source of truth for product, accessibility framing, geometry and QNX mechanism; supersedes the Nov 20 build plan; ops live in docs/team-plan.md.

nodes.label: Five-process QNX isolation architecture
nodes.rationale: Microkernel story: separate address spaces, FIFO/RR priorities, runmasks, supervisor and seqlocked shm so `slay percept` cannot mute the piezo. Do not collapse into one binary.

nodes.label: QNX 8.0 has no Adaptive Partitioning (APS)
nodes.rationale: APS is unsupported on QNX 8.0, so mixed criticality is built from processes, priorities, runmasks, a supervisor and seqlocked shm. Do not pitch APS.

nodes.label: Pitch language and framing guidance
nodes.rationale: Avoid cure, tragedy and safety framing; say supplement to the cane, baked word list, sighted team, not BLV-tested.

nodes.label: CPU runmask core-0 isolation (0x1 vs 0xe)
nodes.rationale: Model thread pools (ORT/TFLite/MediaPipe) must not migrate onto core 0; ThreadCtl runmask on every created thread because spawn runmask is not enough.

nodes.label: First empirical gates (busy-loop, tape, YOLOE p95, MediaPipe hit rate, synonym table)
nodes.norm_label: first empirical gates (busy-loop, tape, yoloe p95, mediapipe hit rate, synonym table)

nodes.label: camd camera daemon (FIFO 50, core 0)
nodes.rationale: Stays on core 0 so Sensor Framework callbacks are not scheduled behind ORT; no colour convert, no net, no invented frames.

nodes.label: Startup after io-audio / Sensor Framework (not /boot/onboot)
nodes.rationale: /boot/onboot runs before pipes and /usr exist, so it cannot launch Beacon.

nodes.label: P2: Other notes (LRU objects, ground-plane, focus lock, AGPL)
nodes.norm_label: p2: other notes (lru objects, ground-plane, focus lock, agpl)

nodes.label: Tape-measure depth gate (>30% error mutes metres)
nodes.norm_label: tape-measure depth gate (>30% error mutes metres)

nodes.label: Range 2: object still in view (walk while looking, no VO)
nodes.norm_label: range 2: object still in view (walk while looking, no vo)

nodes.label: RETURN ('take me back') breadcrumb retrace
nodes.rationale: Gated on Saturday VO p95; never faked from a log; a short retrace of this walk, not indoor navigation.

nodes.label: Merge verdict: BLOCK
nodes.rationale: Product locks were right but the draft was not buildable: LIVE/HOLD aging false on its own proxy, REACH geometry not closed, shm not a multi-writer contract, 'refill water' did not bind, script argued with cut order, Nov 20 plan still pointed at AprilTags.

nodes.norm_label: p0: live < 300 ms incompatible with capture-time aging

nodes.norm_label: p1: nov 20 build plan conflicts (apriltag, walk ticks, yolo11n)

nodes.label: P1: 'Refill water' does not resolve to stored bottle
nodes.norm_label: p1: 'refill water' does not resolve to stored bottle

nodes.label: Mode LIVE / HOLD / LOST
nodes.rationale: Computed only in guided. LIVE = latest bundle contains the name and age < max(1.0 s, 2x p95); HOLD up to 1.5 s with no new metres; LOST never speaks a number. Silence and a fake distance are both unusable.

nodes.label: slay percept -> HOLD -> LOST failure demo
nodes.norm_label: slay percept -> hold -> lost failure demo
nodes.rationale: The QNX prize beat: a high-priority thread on core 0 still makes sound after the detector is dead; honest 'I lost the target'.

nodes.label: WALK guidance law (spoken instruction)
nodes.rationale: Walking is speech so a cane hand is not fighting beeps; WALK ticks from the Nov 20 design are removed.

nodes.label: MediaPipe hands (palm + landmark lite)
nodes.rationale: Runs in percept, off the 16 ms guided thread; the 5-10 ms claim is unsourced.

nodes.label: QNX AI workshop (MediaPipe hands on Pi)
nodes.norm_label: qnx ai workshop (mediapipe hands on pi)

nodes.label: Range 1: same camera frame (tabletop reach, no VO)
nodes.norm_label: range 1: same camera frame (tabletop reach, no vo)
nodes.rationale: frame_id check required because chest rotation between object and hand updates makes camera-frame subtraction wrong.

nodes.label: P0: Geometry not closed (no depth shm, no letterbox/crop inverses)
nodes.norm_label: p0: geometry not closed (no depth shm, no letterbox/crop inverses)

nodes.label: P1: 16 ms guided deadline vs MediaPipe and USB writes on core 0
nodes.norm_label: p1: 16 ms guided deadline vs mediapipe and usb writes on core 0

nodes.label: Off-axis tick amplitude floor (~0.25)
nodes.rationale: Losing the sound off-axis was the main failure in the 12-person BLV hand-steering study, so ticks never go silent while REACH is live.

nodes.label: REACH guidance law (ticks only)
nodes.rationale: Enter at |d| <= 0.50 m for 3 frames with LIVE mode and confident hand, exit at >= 0.70 m; hysteresis on the law; the only time ticks run.

nodes.label: /beacon_depth depth slot (shm)
nodes.rationale: Required: REACH cannot unproject a fingertip without depth, the depth/yolo letterbox affines and the hand crop.

nodes.label: /beacon_frames newest-frame ring (shm)
nodes.rationale: Three slots, newest wins, drop on overrun; copied from MOGGIE/EyeMelody newest-frame pattern.

nodes.label: objects[32] session POI store
nodes.rationale: Rows are not deleted when they leave the camera (that is the session map); LRU-evict unused non-target rows, never the current target.

nodes.label: percept vision process (RR 22, cores 1-3)
nodes.rationale: Best effort; may die. Restart attaches to /beacon_world without zeroing objects or crumbs. Proposes objects[]; does not write target.

nodes.label: pose_epoch
nodes.rationale: Bumped on percept restart so ghost xyz from a previous epoch cannot win 'nearest'.

nodes.label: Range 3: object out of view / RETURN (needs world pose)
nodes.norm_label: range 3: object out of view / return (needs world pose)

nodes.label: RGB-D visual odometry (ORB + solvePnPRansac)
nodes.rationale: Not SLAM or loop closure; one metric chain so a point stored ten seconds ago can be aimed at after a turn. Fails to pose.valid=0, never invents motion.

nodes.label: target (guided-owned bind)
nodes.rationale: Single target author is guided; geometry copied from objects[] at bind time; mode is not stored.

nodes.label: P1: WorldState has three writers and one seq
nodes.norm_label: p1: worldstate has three writers and one seq

nodes.label: Seqlock with per-writer seq
nodes.rationale: guided never blocks on a mutex percept might hold when it dies; one global seq over a multi-writer blob is not a contract.

nodes.label: guided synthesizer (FIFO 58, core 0)
nodes.rationale: Synthesizer only: no models, no full-frame convert, no blocking USB write, so it never waits on ONNX, whisper, llama or MediaPipe.

nodes.label: Heartbeat pulses and supervisor 50 ms timer
nodes.norm_label: heartbeat pulses and supervisor 50 ms timer

nodes.label: procmgr_ability priority ability and root drop
nodes.norm_label: procmgr_ability priority ability and root drop

nodes.label: voiced speech process (RR 18, cores 1-3)
nodes.rationale: Writes intent only; forbidden from writing metres, headings, target, objects or playing USB audio.

nodes.label: Candidate-set bind to stored objects
nodes.rationale: Table returns a job plus a candidate set so 'refill water' binds a stored bottle; never pick a class outside the set (NACK_UNSEEN).

nodes.label: QNX message passing (MsgSend / pulses) for edges only
nodes.norm_label: qnx message passing (msgsend / pulses) for edges only
nodes.rationale: Not the frame path; guided must never MsgSend to percept and wait, which would invert the priority story.

nodes.label: Saturday Build Order (spec section 13, steps 1-6)
nodes.rationale: Bring up the 60 Hz guided loop under load first, then calibration, REACH, FIND, and the honest-failure path; VO and RETURN only if steps 1-5 are green, with feature freeze Saturday midnight.

nodes.label: Hardware Request (Camera Module 3, USB headset, piezo)
nodes.norm_label: hardware request (camera module 3, usb headset, piezo)

nodes.label: Lane C: ORB+PnP VO and RETURN
nodes.norm_label: lane c: orb+pnp vo and return

nodes.label: Aural and Haptic Feedback for Visually Impaired People on a Track (ICHI)
nodes.norm_label: aural and haptic feedback for visually impaired people on a track (ichi)

nodes.label: Open-Ear / Non-Occluding Audio
nodes.rationale: 14/15 PVI wanted non-occluding audio and cane users struggle with body vibration and low-frequency sound; the spec's USB headset is a safety/acceptability question, so test one-ear, bone-conduction and open-ear options.

nodes.label: RETURN Is Not Indoor Navigation
nodes.rationale: NavCog error and overload findings support a short optional retrace, not a general 'take me anywhere' navigation claim.

nodes.label: Logitech C270 Stand-In Camera and Mic
nodes.norm_label: logitech c270 stand-in camera and mic
nodes.rationale: If parts are late the C270 can stand in through build step 5 when it appears on Sensor Framework, but its W x H must not be written into beacon.h.

nodes.label: include/beacon.h Shared Header
nodes.rationale: Frozen first from current spec section 6 so everyone builds against one contract; must not hardcode C270 CAM_W/CAM_H.

nodes.label: Replay Generator (.jsonl samples)
nodes.rationale: Writes a reach, a HOLD and a LOST into laptop/samples so dashboard work is never blocked on hardware.

nodes.label: telemd (read-only telemetry process)
nodes.rationale: Optional lowest-priority sixth process (runmask 0xe), read-only on shm with seqlock readers, never writes shm or talks to guided; sends world JSON ~10 Hz and JPEG ~5 fps over local UDP, not a cloud path.

nodes.label: Privacy Concerns with Be My Eyes / Aira (SOUPS 2019 poster)
nodes.norm_label: privacy concerns with be my eyes / aira (soups 2019 poster)

nodes.label: On-Device Processing for Privacy
nodes.rationale: No camera feed sent to a stranger addresses documented BLV privacy concerns about human-powered visual assistance; whether a chest camera still worries bystanders is open.

nodes.label: Dashboard Non-Interference Rule
nodes.rationale: The laptop dashboard is additive and never on the wearer's path: kill telemd or unplug the laptop mid-demo and the wearer hears no difference.

nodes.label: Guidance Laws (STOP, LOST, REACH, WALK, RETURN)
nodes.norm_label: guidance laws (stop, lost, reach, walk, return)

nodes.label: REPEAT / REJECT Intents
nodes.rationale: REPEAT replays the last cue and REJECT tries the next candidate; test phrases include 'say that again' and 'not that one'.

nodes.label: Auditory Hand-Steering Guidance for BLV People (CHI 2026)
nodes.norm_label: auditory hand-steering guidance for blv people (chi 2026)

nodes.label: Evaluation of Short-Range Depth Sonifications (IEEE THMS)
nodes.norm_label: evaluation of short-range depth sonifications (ieee thms)

nodes.label: UI Preferences for a Camera-Based Wayfinding Aid (JVIB)
nodes.norm_label: ui preferences for a camera-based wayfinding aid (jvib)

nodes.label: Repeat / Wrong-One / Cancel Affordance
nodes.rationale: BLV users want to question and refine output; repeat-last-cue, 'that's the wrong one' and cancel should be first-class voice commands alongside STOP.

nodes.label: Off-Axis Search Cue
nodes.rationale: Losing the sound entirely when the hand is off-axis was the main sonification failure mode ('like a guessing game'), so an always-findable off-axis cue is required.

nodes.label: Parsimonious, Query-Driven Instructions
nodes.rationale: Blind participants prefer querying over continuous speech and brief action-timed cues; streams of corrections raise cognitive load and mask environmental sound, so do not narrate the room while walking.

nodes.label: Tick Rate as Distance Encoding
nodes.rationale: Beep repetition rate was the most learnable and memorable depth encoding (sighted-blindfolded evidence only); rate means closer, so errors or LOST must use a different timbre, never a faster tick.

nodes.label: WALK Speech / REACH Ticks Audio Split
nodes.norm_label: walk speech / reach ticks audio split
nodes.rationale: CHI 2026 hand-steering study: speech is faster for coarse guidance, sonification has far lower error for fine near-field work; so short speech on WALK and ticks only during REACH.

nodes.label: Pi 5 CPU Frame Budget (YOLO11n 168 ms + depth 120 ms)
nodes.norm_label: pi 5 cpu frame budget (yolo11n 168 ms + depth 120 ms)
nodes.rationale: QNX baseline is YOLO11n ONNX 320 px ~168 ms plus depth ~120 ms, everything else is additive; no stack leaves room for a second 200 ms CLIP pass.

nodes.label: Depth Anything V2 Metric Indoor Small
nodes.norm_label: depth anything v2 metric indoor small

nodes.label: supervisor (spawn, runmasks, heartbeats, restarts)
nodes.rationale: The only process started by hand on the Pi; it spawns the rest, restarts with backoff and owns the piezo fault path.

nodes.label: llama.cpp + Qwen2.5-0.5B GGUF Fallback Remap
nodes.rationale: llama.cpp is a real QNX port (CPU-only ggml); 0.5B Qwen runs ~12-34 tok/s on Pi 5, i.e. ~1-2 s for a 16-token remap, acceptable only off the hot loop and strictly text-to-text.

nodes.label: Session POI Store (label, xyz, t, conf)
nodes.norm_label: session poi store (label, xyz, t, conf)
nodes.rationale: For a small session-scoped store, label string plus 3D centroid plus timestamp is enough; a CLIP or vector index is not justified (LOST-3DSG used ~3 KB vs ~641 MB for per-voxel CLIP).

nodes.label: Deterministic Synonym Query Remap
nodes.rationale: Query-time remap such as 'refill water' to fountain / water dispenser / sink / bottle via a table first, with a tiny text-only LLM only as fallback; mirrors how NLMap and EPG bridge language to structured 3D data. Remap quality is untested.

nodes.label: Depth Anything V2 Metric Indoor Small INT8
nodes.norm_label: depth anything v2 metric indoor small int8

nodes.label: llama.cpp ~0.5B remap (table miss only)
nodes.rationale: Must not emit numbers; distances and headings never come from the LLM.

nodes.label: P1: SoC budget is not simultaneous cadences; three journeys oversold
nodes.norm_label: p1: soc budget is not simultaneous cadences; three journeys oversold

nodes.label: Baked 16-32 noun list (open-vocab = no retraining)
nodes.rationale: A product limit, not an implementation detail; the MobileCLIP text encoder never ships to the Pi.

nodes.label: Sequential percept pipeline (YOLO -> depth -> hands -> VO)
nodes.norm_label: sequential percept pipeline (yolo -> depth -> hands -> vo)
nodes.rationale: Proxy ms are not simultaneous cadences; combined ~2-3 Hz expected; parallel YOLO||depth only after a measured loaner p95. 60 Hz guided != 60 fresh 3D samples.

nodes.label: AirTag Precision Finding
nodes.rationale: Works well but requires tagging, a holder, specific UWB iPhones; coarse VoiceOver directions and room/floor ambiguity break trust.

nodes.label: No-Tag Homing
nodes.rationale: Removes the pairing, holder, phone and UWB prerequisites BLV reviewers identify as AirTag friction, but only works for items the camera has actually seen.

nodes.label: AI Proposes, High-Priority Thread Disposes
nodes.rationale: Architecture is a good honesty story only if the wearer-facing claim matches: sensors give a measured bearing and the device says when it no longer has one.

nodes.label: Multi-Purpose Camera Apps (Seeing AI, Lookout, Be My Eyes, Envision)
nodes.norm_label: multi-purpose camera apps (seeing ai, lookout, be my eyes, envision)
nodes.rationale: Snapshot/verification tools, not homing tools: users cannot perceive framing problems, hallucinations and cultural misfit are common, and errors are unverifiable.

nodes.label: Floor-Level Dropped Items Scope Gap
nodes.rationale: Dropped medication on the floor is a cited pain point but may be outside the chest camera's tabletop geometry; do not demo a floor drop unless tested.

nodes.label: Inclusive Language and Non-Cure Framing
nodes.rationale: Use 'people who are blind or have low vision', respect self-identification, and frame Beacon as access to a specific action rather than restored sight; cure rhetoric and safety/navigation claims are explicitly avoided.

nodes.label: Independence as Control, Not Avoiding Help
nodes.norm_label: independence as control, not avoiding help
nodes.rationale: Asking for help is not itself a loss of independence; loss of control over when and how help arrives is. Avoid 'no more asking for help' framing.

nodes.label: Tactile-First Problem-Solving Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: BLV people try themselves, use touch and memory, and use digital tools last; Beacon should complement tactile strategies and position itself for moved items or uncontrolled spaces, not replace a consistent home.

nodes.norm_label: this is my fault, really? blv perception of lvlm hallucination (uist 2025)

nodes.label: No BLV Validation / Codesign Gap
nodes.rationale: Top product risk: no BLV tester was involved in the locked spec; parachute design is a recurring failure mode, so the pitch must say 'prototype, not yet validated with BLV wearers' and plan paid BLV-led testing.

nodes.label: Categorical Audible Uncertainty
nodes.rationale: BLV participants split on numeric confidence and prefer hedged, tone-based or tiered (high/uncertain/withheld) uncertainty; calibrated honesty cut overconfident wrong assertions from ~11% to ~3%.

nodes.label: Honest LOST Cue (no invented metres)
nodes.rationale: Answers hallucination, overtrust and unverifiable-error findings: a distinct earcon plus a short sentence with no number when perception is lost; never speak metres from stale frames and never go silent. Exact sound and HOLD duration remain unvalidated with BLV users.

nodes.label: Named-Object Homing (Beacon core job)
nodes.rationale: Strongest unmet BLV need is finding, disambiguating and physically reaching a specific personal item without waiting for a sighted helper; object-finding is the largest failure category of camera apps, so Beacon homes to a named object instead of narrating scenes.

nodes.label: Default qnxuser Password Risk
nodes.rationale: Until passwd is run interactively on the device, anyone on the hotspot can log in as qnxuser and sudo to root.

nodes.label: Read-Only IFS Image (qnx_sdp.ifs)
nodes.rationale: Cannot be rebuilt without mkifs from the QNX SDP, so treat it as immutable.

nodes.label: QNX Process Idioms (pidin, slay)
nodes.rationale: No systemd: list with pidin ar, kill or restart with slay -f; processes started from SSH die with the session unless detached.

nodes.label: QNXE-1894 Wi-Fi Settings Copy Bug
nodes.rationale: Timestamp-gated copy of /boot/wpa_supplicant.conf to /data/var/etc/settings can fail, leaving bcm0 associated on a 169.254.x.x address; fixed by cat-ing the /boot copies in onboot every boot plus future timestamps.

nodes.label: qnxpi Target (QNX 8.0 Raspberry Pi 5)
nodes.rationale: Not a normal Linux box: read-only IFS image, QNX6 data partition, no systemd, apt or bash guarantees; most traps follow from these facts.

nodes.label: slog2info / slogger2 Logging
nodes.rationale: Per-buffer system logs usually explain an instant process exit within seconds; check them before adding prints.

nodes.label: Two Pi Build Loops (qcc cross-build / on-device make)
nodes.norm_label: two pi build loops (qcc cross-build / on-device make)

nodes.label: Pi Development Workflow (QNX 8.0 on Raspberry Pi 5)
nodes.norm_label: pi development workflow (qnx 8.0 on raspberry pi 5)

nodes.label: /data QNX6 Partition
nodes.rationale: Only large writable space that survives reboot and holds /home; /etc lives on the system partition shared with QNX and is wiped by reflash, so owned code and config go in /data.

nodes.label: rsync + make Build-on-Device Loop
nodes.rationale: Device has gcc, make, git, python3.14 and pip3; rsyncing the tree and running make over SSH is fast enough for a hackathon and avoids configuring a QNX SDP cross-toolchain on the host.

nodes.label: mDNS Fallthrough to home.lab (IP-Pinned SSH Alias)
nodes.norm_label: mdns fallthrough to home.lab (ip-pinned ssh alias)
nodes.rationale: qnxpi.local never reaches glibc and falls through to an unrelated tailnet host, so the ssh alias is pinned to the IP and must be updated if the lease changes.

nodes.label: /boot/onboot Boot Hook
nodes.rationale: Only hook that runs before the network, but it runs before the pipe component and before /usr is mounted: no pipes or command substitution, only /proc/boot utilities; long work goes in a sleeping background child; logs go to /boot/onboot.log. Used for Wi-Fi and hostname only, never to launch Beacon.

nodes.label: Supervisor Startup via SLM post_startup
nodes.rationale: Start supervisor from a snippet ordered after io-audio, Sensor Framework and /usr (QSTI post_startup or an SLM component), because /boot/onboot runs before pipes and /usr exist (spec section 5.1).

nodes.label: USB SD Card Reader Workflow
nodes.rationale: The laptop's internal rtsx_pci reader drops its PCIe link within minutes and needs a cold boot to recover; a USB reader stays usable.

nodes.label: QNX Calls Behind #ifdef __QNX__
nodes.rationale: ThreadCtl, procmgr_ability, pulses, CamAPI and GPIO are guarded so every process also builds and runs on a laptop for parallel development before hardware arrives.
